meta.tagline: From bougainvillea lanes to turquoise depths — Lycia's calm harbor

pills: The Lycian Way passes the door

overview.title: Welcome to Kas
overview.intro: Kas is an old Lycian town where the Taurus mountains drop straight into the sea, its bougainvillea-wrapped white houses facing the harbor like an amphitheater. There are no big hotels, no crowded beaches; instead there are turquoise coves, ancient rock tombs, the Lycian Way passing the door, and Turkey's clearest diving waters. The Greek island of Kastellorizo sits a stone's throw across the water, and a little further along, the sunken city of Kekova sleeps beneath the surface. Kas is a town for the unhurried: you swim in the morning, stretch out in the shade at noon, and in the evening life begins again on the square.

local_word.definition: Turkish's untranslatable word: the conscious, contented state of doing nothing. Kas is its capital — tea at the harbor, a book in bougainvillea shade, silence at sunset. If someone says 'keyfine bak' ('mind your keyif'), they've just recited the town's constitution to you.

rules.title: Go to Kaputas early or don't rush at all
rules.description: Turkey's most photographed beach fills by noon: between 08:00 and 10:00 the turquoise is all yours. If you arrive at midday, don't force it — quiet coves with the same water are nearby; save Kaputas for tomorrow morning.

rules.title: Look beneath the sea at least once
rules.description: Kas is Turkey's diving capital: visibility reaches 30 meters, and wrecks and reefs are next-door neighbors. Never dived? A discovery dive is the perfect place to start — at minimum, take a mask and snorkel out to the Limanagzi coves; the underwater world is half of Kas.

rules.title: Walk one trail, and let Lycia walk with you
rules.description: The Lycian Way passes through town: marked routes lead to the ancient theater, cliff views and olive-grove paths. Give one morning to a hike — in shoes, not sandals, with water in your bag. Lycia's stones tell stories.

quick_facts.label: Scale
quick_facts.sub: Square, harbor, beach — all on foot

tip.label: The Kas philosophy
tip.text: In Kas the plan should be small and the keyif large: start the day with a swim, leave noon to the shade, save the evening for the square. You come here not with a to-do list but with the freedom not to do.

transport.title: Getting Around Town and the Coves
transport.intro: Reaching Kas takes patience — both airports are far; once you arrive, everything is within walking, dolmus or boat distance.

items.title: Arriving from the airports
items.description: Dalaman and Antalya airports are 2.5–3 hours away: airport buses and transfers run steadily. The road is long but the D400 coastal highway earns forgiveness with its views — ask for the window seat.

items.title: A walkable town
items.description: The square, harbor, ancient theater and Kucukcakil beach are all within walking distance: most days a car is unnecessary in Kas. The bougainvillea slopes of the Long Bazaar are the town's main artery — comfortable shoes beat flip-flops.

items.title: Dolmus minibuses
items.description: Minibuses run all day toward Kaputas and Kalkan: hop on with your beach bag, and in twenty minutes you're in turquoise. The Cukurbag peninsula loop dolmus is handy for the hotels — ask the driver about return times.

items.title: Boats and the captains' cooperative
items.description: Daily boats leave the harbor for Kekova: the sunken city, Kalekoy and swimming stops included. A small boat beats a big one — talk at the cooperative stand and choose your captain.

items.title: The Kastellorizo ferry
items.description: The ferry to the Greek island of Meis (Kastellorizo) across the water takes twenty minutes: a day trip with your passport. Colorful harbor houses, Greek tavernas and the blue cave tour — Turkey's shortest trip abroad.

callout.label: Kekova tip
callout.text: Board an early Kekova boat: by noon the boats queue up over the sunken city. The morning boat finds the sea calm and reaches Kalekoy before the crowds — and the climb to Simena castle is far sweeter in the morning cool.

stay.title: Where to Stay
stay.intro: In Kas, choosing where to stay means choosing a scale: a pansiyon above the square, a seafront hotel on the peninsula, a view terrace in Kalkan, or a stone house in a village.

local_word.definition: A small family-run guesthouse: the soul of Kas lives in the pansiyon, not the big hotel. Breakfast comes to the courtyard with homemade jam, and tips come from the host, not a reception desk — within three days you're promoted from guest to friend.

items.name: Kas center
items.description: Pansiyons and boutique hotels on the bougainvillea lanes: you walk down to the square, the harbor and the evening life. The natural address for those who want to feel the town's rhythm.

items.name: Cukurbag Peninsula
items.description: Seafront hotels on the peninsula five minutes from town: you leap into turquoise from ladder-down platforms. The sunset view is this side's signature — the quiet, scenic option.

items.name: Around Kucukcakil
items.description: The town's beach quarter: swim in the morning, be at breakfast in two minutes, walk to the square at night. The densest cluster of hotels and pansiyons — a balanced, practical choice.

items.name: Kalkan
items.description: The neighboring town twenty minutes away: a more polished alternative with white houses, rooftop restaurants and marina views. It's even closer to Kaputas than Kas is — splitting your stay between the two towns is a strategy of its own.

items.name: Lycian villages
items.description: Stone houses and mountain cool in Islamlar and the surrounding villages: crickets at night, roosters at dawn. A peaceful base if you have a car — fifteen minutes to the sea, zero to serenity.

best_time.title: When to Go
best_time.intro: The sea at Kas is open from May to November; spring and autumn belong to the trails, summer to the sea, winter to the silence.

items.label: Spring
items.name: Lycian Spring
items.subtitle: Spring · Trail season, warming turquoise
items.description: The golden season of the Lycian Way: the trails are in flower, the weather is made for hiking, and by May the sea is swimmable. The town is calm, the pansiyons easygoing — this is the hiker's and early-season traveler's Kas.

callout.label: May tip
callout.text: In May: a Lycian trail in the morning, the first swim at noon, a quiet square at night — a triple that's impossible in summer crowds is daily routine this month. The dive schools are in their calm season too — an ideal window for a discovery dive.

items.label: Summer
items.name: Turquoise Peak
items.subtitle: Summer · Clearest sea, full square, warm nights
items.description: The sea is at its clearest and the nights at their liveliest: the square lives late, the coves fill with boat chatter. Hot middays call for shade — beach in the morning, keyif at noon, square at night is summer's constitution.

callout.label: Booking note
callout.text: In July–August, Kas's smallness works in reverse: pansiyons and dinner tables fill early. Book your stay weeks ahead and reserve your favorite restaurant by afternoon — the town is small, the demand is large.

items.label: Autumn
items.name: September Clarity
items.subtitle: Autumn · Warm sea, emptying coves
items.description: September and October are Kas at its wisest setting: the sea keeps its summer warmth, the crowds recede, and diving visibility peaks. Even in November you can swim on a sunny day — and the trails live their second spring.

callout.label: October tip
callout.text: In October there's no queue for the Kekova boat, Kaputas mornings are nearly private, and the water is still warm. Summer prices retreat — this is the month for those who want Kas at its most Kas.

items.label: Winter
items.name: The Quiet Harbor
items.subtitle: Winter · Local rhythm, sunny calm days
items.description: In winter Kas belongs to its locals and its wintering foreigners: the square's cafes hum with conversation, and the D400's views turn empty and majestic. Sitting on the theater steps on a sunny winter day is a program in itself — a rainy day is for books and keyif.

callout.label: February tip
callout.text: February is orange and lemon season: the market stalls turn citrus, and the trails are deserted. Watching the sunset alone at the ancient theater — a summer fantasy, a winter routine.

eat.title: What to Eat
eat.intro: The Kas table is the Mediterranean itself: the day's fish, olive-oil wild greens, meze plates and evenings that stretch long under the bougainvillea.

local_word.definition: The table's great art of small plates: from sea beans to fava, smoky eggplant to cured bonito. In Kas, meze is the evening itself — plates are shared, raki is sipped slowly, conversation stretches. The rule is simple: order few, and reorder what you love.

items.name: Catch of the day
items.description: Grouper, sea bream, sea bass or gurnard in season: chosen from the display, cooked over coals. The lokantas behind the harbor sell by weight — ask the price before the scale, order it simple with lemon.
items.tag: Choose from the display · off the coals

items.name: Olive-oil wild greens
items.description: Sea beans, şevketibostan, pickled rock samphire: Mediterranean greens in olive oil are the table's foundation. Ask to see the meze fridge — the season's greens are announced by the fridge, not the menu.

items.name: Calamari and octopus
items.description: A diving town takes its seafood seriously: grilled octopus and crisp calamari are every meyhane's pride plate. Grilled beats fried — squeeze the lemon, take your time.
items.tag: Meyhane classic · ask for it grilled

items.name: Village breakfast
items.description: A spread breakfast in the courtyard: goat cheese, olive varieties, homemade jams, griddle borek and well-steeped tea. The long ritual of a Kas morning — a second round after a swim is entirely legitimate.

items.name: Cop sis and village kebab
items.description: Marinated lamb on the thinnest skewers: the craft of village lokantas along the D400 and the town's masters. A carnivorous pause between sea meals — with charred peppers and tandoor bread alongside.

items.name: Semolina halva with ice cream
items.description: Hot semolina halva meeting cold ice cream: the classic close of a Kas evening. With pistachios for those who want them — this is the last plate before the square stroll.

callout.label: Table rule
callout.text: The front-row harbor-view tables write the view into the bill: one street inland, the same meze table costs friendlier money. With fish, season is everything — ask where the boat captains eat, and the answer walks you to the right door.

hidden_gems.title: Hidden Corners
hidden_gems.intro: Everyone knows the Kaputas photo; these six are Kas's hidden blues.

items.name: Limanagzi
items.description: The coves on the peninsula across the harbor, reached only by boat or footpath: small jetty beaches, crystal water, Lycian rock tombs on the ridge behind. Five minutes by water taxi — the antidote to crowds.

items.name: Kalekoy (Simena)
items.description: A coastal village with no road, unreachable without a boat: a path climbing to a Lycian castle, sarcophagi half-sunk in the sea, gozleme scenting the jetty. The Kekova view from the castle is among the Mediterranean's finest frames.

items.name: Aperlai
items.description: An ancient Lycian harbor reached on foot or by boat on the Sicak peninsula: city walls, quay stones half underwater, and barely a boat in sight. Snorkeling above an ancient quay — the Kas version of time travel.

items.name: Meis (Kastellorizo)
items.description: The colorful Greek town on the opposite shore: twenty minutes by ferry, a day trip with a passport. Harbor tavernas, the blue cave boat and pastel facades — the island you keep gazing at from Kas is even lovelier up close.

items.name: Patara
items.description: Half an hour away, 12 kilometers of unbroken sand: the columns of ancient Patara stand at the beach's gate. Kept unbuilt as a loggerhead turtle nesting ground — at sunset the dunes turn to gold.

items.name: Sunset at the ancient theater
items.description: The steps of the Hellenistic theater in the middle of town face the sea: at dusk, locals and those in the know gather quietly. No ticket, no gate — just stone, sea and the sinking sun.

callout.label: Cove strategy
callout.text: The key to Kas's hidden coves is the morning: catch the Limanagzi water taxi at 09:00, start the Aperlai trail early, see Kaputas at 08:00. By the time the midday crowd arrives, you're already at your second cove.

traps.title: Tourist Traps
traps.intro: Kas is a small, honest town, but its summer showcase isn't without games; know these four and keep your keyif unbroken.

items.name: Arriving at Kaputas at noon
items.description: Turkey's most photographed beach becomes a staircase-to-sunbed queue in the midday hours; the turquoise is the same, the experience is not.
items.instead: Go between 08:00 and 10:00: clear water, empty sand, ideal light. If it's already noon, turn around and take the Limanagzi water taxi — the same blue, a tenth of the crowd.

items.name: The big-boat crowd
items.description: On hundred-person boats, the Kekova tour becomes a loudspeaker parade; boats queue up over the sunken city.
items.instead: Choose a small boat from the cooperative or share a private one with a few people: fewer passengers, longer swim stops, a calmer route. A morning departure always beats noon.

items.name: The unagreed taxi ride
items.description: On airport and cove transfers the price sometimes turns into a 'surprise' after you're in; the night tariff can be creatively interpreted.
items.instead: Fix the price before you get in, or arrange transfers through your hotel: shared airport shuttles are far more economical. Within town, everything is walking distance anyway.

items.name: Arriving in summer without a plan
items.description: In July–August the pansiyons fill months ahead; last-minute arrivals are left with expensive, soulless options outside town.
items.instead: Book summer accommodation early; if you're flexible, choose the May–June or September–October window. The same Kas awaits you at half the price and a quarter of the crowd.

callout.label: Golden rule
callout.text: The code to a good Kas experience is early hours and small scale: morning beach, small boat, pansiyon table. Return when the crowd leaves; don't go where it goes at noon — the town will thank you.

itinerary.title: Ready-Made Itineraries
itinerary.intro: If you hate planning, follow these flows. Times are flexible; keep the spirit, break the order.

plans.title: If You Have 1 Day
plans.subtitle: From turquoise morning to a night on the square

steps.title: Kaputas morning
steps.description: Twenty minutes by dolmus: descend the stairs and swim while the turquoise is still empty. The morning light does the beach justice.

steps.title: Long breakfast
steps.description: Back in town, sit down to a courtyard pansiyon breakfast: goat cheese, homemade jam, steeped tea. Hurrying forbidden — that's the Kas constitution.

steps.title: Long Bazaar and the rock tombs
steps.description: Shop-browsing on the bougainvillea slopes; a short climb to the Lycian tombs carved into the cliff above. A midday of shade breaks and ice cream.

steps.title: Limanagzi escape
steps.description: Cross the harbor by water taxi in five minutes: swim at the jetty cove, stretch out on a sunbed. Ask the captain about the return boat times.

steps.title: Sunset at the ancient theater
steps.description: Sit on the theater's stone steps: the sun drops into the sea and the town turns orange. Kas's best 'ticket' is free.

steps.title: Meyhane evening and the square
steps.description: Meze plates, fish off the coals, long conversation under the bougainvillea. Close with semolina halva and ice cream on the square — the night ends there.

plans.title: If You Have 3 Days
plans.subtitle: Coves, the sunken city and Lycian trails

steps.title: Classic Kas
steps.description: The 1-day flow above: Kaputas morning, the bazaar, Limanagzi, theater sunset, meyhane.

steps.title: Kekova and the sunken city
steps.description: Morning boat to Kekova: glide over the sunken city, climb to Simena castle at Kalekoy, swimming stops in the coves. Evening sunset on the Cukurbag peninsula and a waterfront dinner.

steps.title: The Lycian Way and Patara
steps.description: A morning hike on the Kas stage of the Lycian Way in the cool hours; the ancient city + 12-kilometer beach at Patara in the afternoon; meet the sunset on the dunes, and set your farewell table at a rooftop restaurant in Kalkan.

phrases.title: 5-Word Survival Kit
phrases.intro: Mediterranean people are warm and words open doors; these five guarantee tables and conversation in Kas.

items.meaning: 'Welcome' — the first phrase you'll hear at the pansiyon door; the reply is 'hoş bulduk'
Article one of the Kas constitution — 'relax, enjoy yourself'
'Enjoy your meal' — opens and closes the meze table; the fisherman and the breakfast cook both say it
'Health to your hands' — the finest thank-you to the cook; say it to the meze maker and the plates grow generous
'Cheers!' — as glasses rise under the bougainvillea; the official word of a Mediterranean evening
